questions.question: Which one of the following is a monetary principle stating that "bad money drives out good"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e __**Gresham's law**__

 
• Gresham's law **states that “bad money drives out the good money**”.
 
• **Good money** here means **any currency or coin whose accepted value (legal tender value) and the value of the commodity from which it is made does not differ much**.
 
• **Bad money** means the **coin or currency whose accepted value (legal tender value) is much higher than the value of the commodity from which it is made.**
 
• For example-
 
 
• If a coin has a legal tender value of Rs 100 and the silver metal worth Rs 100 is used to make the coin, then it will be considered as good money in Gresham’s law.
 
• If a coin has a legal tender value of Rs 100 and the alloy worth Rs 5 is used to make the coin, then it will be considered as bad money in Gresham’s law.
 
 
 
• Thus, he said that if both kinds of money are available with the public, having the same legal tender value, then people would start hoarding good money and would use bad money for the transaction.
 
• So, as per our example, people will start hoarding silver coins for their intrinsic value and start using alloy coins for transactions.
 
• Thus, eventually, bad money will drive out good money.
 
 
 

**Pareto efficiency:**

 
• Pareto's efficiency is defined as the economic situation when the **circumstances of one individual cannot be made better without making the situation worse for another individual.**

**Marshall's scissors analysis**

 
• This combined the demand and supply i.e **utility and cost of production.**

**Multiplier Effect**

 
• The multiplier effect refers to the increase in final income arising from any new injection of spending.

questions.question: The power to enquire into and decide all doubts and disputes arising out of election of the President is vested in:
questions.solution:

questions.question: Which force helps swimmers float in water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e __**Buoyant force**__

__CONCEPT:__

__
 
• Archimedes' principle states that when a body immersed in a fluid, whether fully or partially submerged, the upward buoyant force that is exerted on it, is equal to the weight of the fluid that the body displaces.
 
• When an object is submerged in fluid fully or partially, an upward force is exerted on the body. This force is known as the buoyant force. Fbuoyant = ρf Vf g 

where ρf is the density of the fluid in which the object is submerged, Vf is the volume of the displaced fluid (or volume of the object that is submerged inside the fluid) and g is the gravitational acceleration.

 
• When an object is submerged in fluid fully or partially there are two forces, 1. buoyant force 2. weight of the object 

and weight of object **W = mg = ρo Vo g** where ρo is the density of the object, Vo is the volume of the object, g is the gravitational acceleration.

 
• 
 
Laws of Floatation: The three conditions required for the body to float on water are:

 

 
• 
 
The weight of the body in the figure is equal to the buoyant force. (c) (d)

 
 
• 
 
The weight of the body is greater than the weight of the fluid displaced i.e. buoyant force. (b)

 
 
• 
 
The weight of the body is less than the weight of the fluid displaced i.e. buoyant force. (a)

 

Buoyant Force:

 
• Buoyancy or upthrust is an upward force which is exerted by a fluid that opposes the weight of an immersed object.
 
• When a body is wholly or partially immersed in a fluid at rest, the fluid exerts pressure on the surface of the body in contact with the fluid. The pressure is greater on lower surfaces of the body than on the upper surfaces as the pressure in a fluid increases with depth. The resultant of all the forces is an upward force called buoyant force.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3857725767d6f71111a3b47b4e20a8ab039cc38729ceed1b50f291383c3ee8b7.png] 

EXPLANATION:__

From the above explanation, we can see that, 

The upward force applied by the fluid on the object when it is submerged in it is called buoyant force.

**How it helps the swimmers:**

 
• Buoyancy is the upward force that acts on the swimmer while they are in the water. The pressure from beneath the swimmer is much greater than the pressure above them which allow the swimmer to float. At the surface of the pool, there is less resistance as the fluid is more resistant than air.
 
• For an object to float, its buoyant force needs to be greater or equal to the weight of the water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f4998aa63a35bcfc09323b9a7bc99e2be902ff64bd3f9f6f4701b02c494b0eb9.png] 

 
• When an object is floating on water surface then weight of an object is Zero
 
• Fnet = FGravity – FBuoyant = 0 [ FGravity = FBuoyant ]

questions.question: Which of the following is the highest award (in the order of precedence) for military services in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e __**Param Vir Chakra**__

__
 
• ​__Gallantry Award is meant for **exceptional courage, valour and dignity.** In India, Gallantry award are given to the personnel of the forces for their exceptional bravery.
 
• After Independence,** the three Gallantry** awards came into force i.e. the **Paramvir Chakra, the Mahavir Chakra and the Veer Chakra.**
 
• The** Gallantry awards** are announced **twice in a year** i.e on **Republic day and on Independence day.**
 
• The order of Precedence of these awards is 

 
• Param Vir Chakra
 
• Ashoka Chakra
 
• Mahavir Chakra
 
• Kirti Chakra
 
• Vir Chakra
 
• Shaurya Chakra

**Param Vir Chakra:**

 
• The Param Vir Chakra is awarded for most conspicuous bravery or some daring or pre-eminent act of valour or self-sacrifice, in the presence of the enemy, whether on land, at sea, or in the air.
 
• Param Vir Chakra means **"Wheel of the Ultimate Brave".**

**Ashok Chakra:**

 
• The Ashok Chakra is **India's highest peacetime military decoration** awarded for valour, courageous action or self-sacrifice away from the battlefield.
 
• It is the peacetime equivalent of the **Param Vir Chakra.**

**Kirti Chakra:**

 
• The Kirti Chakra is an Indian military decoration awarded for valour, courageous action or self-sacrifice away from the field of battle.
 
• It may be awarded to civilians as well as military personnel, including posthumous awards. It is the peacetime equivalent of the Maha Vir Chakra

**Vir Chakra:**

 
• Vir Chakra is an Indian gallantry award presented for acts of gallantry in the presence of the enemy on the battlefield.
